citation: Smith, J. L. M., Nelson, N. J., Smolkowski, K., Baker, S. K., Fien, H., & Kosty, D. (2016). Examining the efficacy of a multitiered intervention for at-risk readers in grade 1. The Elementary School Journal, 116(4), 549-573. https://doi.org/10.1086/686249
report_number: The Elementary School Journal 116(4), 549-573 (ERIC EJ1103958; IES Award R324A090104, Project ECRI, University of Oregon; WWC Study 86383)
design: Cluster-RCT; school-level random assignment blocked by district; 44 elementary schools (22 treatment / 22 control) in Oregon & Massachusetts; analytic sample = 811 grade-1 Tier-2 at-risk readers (394 treatment / 417 control); subject = reading/literacy; intervention = Enhanced Core Reading Instruction (ECRI) = enhanced Tier 1 core reading + aligned Tier 2 small-group intervention + teacher/instructor professional development and coaching, vs business-as-usual core reading + standard district Tier 2.
problems: Full-text PDF read directly from disk (data/fulltext/smith_2016.pdf); the paper reports Hedges' g directly for every Time x condition contrast (Tables 2 and 3), so no recomputation of g was needed. Impacts come from mixed-model (HLM) longitudinal Time x condition analyses with students nested within schools (school = unit of random assignment; 42 df), so they are cluster-adjusted and pretest-adjusted (net fall->spring [or fall->winter] gain difference; time coded 0=T1/1=T2, condition 0=control/1=ECRI). impact_estimate = the Time x condition fixed-effect coefficient (gain-difference in raw test units); impact_se = its model SE. g_se and g_var were derived as g_se = g * (SE_b / b), g_var = g_se^2, consistent with the paper having standardized each g by the spring/winter posttest SD (verified: b/g reproduces the Table 1 posttest SDs to 2 dp, e.g. NWF-WRC 13.82 vs SD 13.9; Word Attack 7.61 vs SD 7.6; SAT-10 Total 29.28 vs SD 29.3; WRMT Word ID 9.54 vs SD 9.5). End-of-treatment (immediate post) wave = SPRING (fall->spring, Table 3, all 7 measures) -> extracted as primary post contrasts. The two WINTER (fall->winter, Table 2) contrasts are an interim mid-year wave covering only NWF-WRC and ORF; they are included and flagged timepoint=winter Y1 / outcome_role=secondary so central logic can drop interim waves. NWF-WRC and ORF appear at both timepoints. Test types: DIBELS NWF/ORF, SAT-10, WRMT Word ID/Word Attack are all standardized/independent published instruments. ICC values are the design ICCs reported per model (school gains, per Murray 1998 p.301). All outcomes are reading -> outcome_subject = Reading. Grade band coded K-2 (grade 1) per registry.

effect_sizes.arm_label: ECRI (enhanced core reading + aligned Tier 2 + PD/coaching) vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.test_name: WRMT Word Attack (Woodcock Reading Mastery Test-revised, Form H)
effect_sizes.timepoint: spring Y1 (end of treatment; fall->spring gain)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g reported by authors (Table 3, Hedges 1981/WWC), from mixed-model Time x condition fall->spring gain difference; standardized by spring posttest SD (~7.6). g_se=g*SE_b/b=0.318*0.91/2.42; g_var=g_se^2.
effect_sizes.notes: Statistically significant favoring ECRI (p=.0112). Largest spring effect. WRMT Word Attack = pseudoword decoding subtest.

effect_sizes.arm_label: ECRI (enhanced core reading + aligned Tier 2 + PD/coaching) vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.test_name: WRMT Word Identification (Woodcock Reading Mastery Test-revised, Form H)
effect_sizes.timepoint: spring Y1 (end of treatment; fall->spring gain)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g reported by authors (Table 3) from mixed-model Time x condition fall->spring gain difference; standardized by spring posttest SD (~9.5). Coefficient 2.24 printed as '2.241' where superscript 1 = p<.10 footnote. g_se=g*SE_b/b=0.235*1.22/2.24; g_var=g_se^2.
effect_sizes.notes: Marginal (p=.0743, p<.10); favors ECRI. Non-significant attributed to larger ICC.

effect_sizes.arm_label: ECRI (enhanced core reading + aligned Tier 2 + PD/coaching) vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.test_name: SAT-10 Word Reading (Stanford Achievement Test, 10th ed.)
effect_sizes.timepoint: spring Y1 (end of treatment; fall->spring gain)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g reported by authors (Table 3) from mixed-model Time x condition fall->spring gain difference (scaled scores); standardized by spring posttest SD (~45.8). g_se=g*SE_b/b=0.235*5.22/10.76; g_var=g_se^2.
effect_sizes.notes: Statistically significant favoring ECRI (p=.0455). Authors note ~4-percentile gain (control 18th -> ECRI ~22nd percentile).
